title: Opening of Drake Passage
summary: Drake Passage, the seaway between South America and Antarctica, opened so that Pacific and Atlantic water could mix at high southern latitudes, and this is linked to the Antarctic Circumpolar Current and to Antarctic glaciation. The date is disputed: earlier estimates ranged from 15 to 49 million years ago, and two studies argue for opening in the mid to late Eocene.

uncertainty.note: Range of 15 to 49 million years ago from the University of Florida news page; individual studies in the sources: mid to late Eocene (Eagles et al. 2006); more than 40 million years (Martin and Scher, per UF). A 2021 Chemical Geology study (31-26 Ma) appeared only in a search result and was not opened.

as_recorded.value: ranged from 15 million years to 49 million years ago

importance.justification: A gateway opening tied to the onset of the Antarctic Circumpolar Current and debated as a cause of Antarctic glaciation.
